paragraphs: The XF P250 is part of the X260 generation, which launched in 2015 and remains in production. It uses the Ingenium AJ200 — a 2.0-litre four-cylinder petrol engine that's part of Jaguar Land Rover's modular engine family. This is the modern petrol unit for the XF range, positioned as the entry-level petrol option alongside the higher-output P300 and the diesel variants. Unlike the diesel-badged X260 variants, which share the Ingenium timing chain pattern, the P250's petrol engine has no independently confirmed wide-scale known issue pattern — it's considered generally reliable within the broader Ingenium family. Jaguar XF P250 Engine Compatibility The XF P250 uses the Ingenium AJ200 petrol engine across the X260 generation, which is a modular design shared with other Jaguar and Land Rover models of the same era. However, the 2.0-litre petrol is a different unit from the diesel version (AJ200D) — they're not interchangeable, and the engine management, fuel system, ancillaries and even the rebuild specifications differ. cards.body: A 3.0-litre inline-six petrol mild-hybrid engine fitted to the XF P250 from 2023 to present. The Ingenium AJ200 features an integrated starter-generator (ISG) and electric auxiliary compressor, making it a more modern and efficient design than the older Ingenium AJ200 V6. We replace timing chains, bearings, water pump and gaskets as standard on every Ingenium AJ200 rebuild.
